attributes.residual: UNCHANGED at real 20 over 48/48. The v2 diagnosis is CONFIRMED verbatim. This record's contribution is the PRECONDITION AUDIT the postprocessor lane needs, plus a correction to the economics. THE THREE FORM SITES all share ONE source register, r29, defined exactly ONCE by `li r29,0` (target 0x14, ours 0x18). Site 1 @0x1c: target `mr r30,r29`, ours `li r30,0`. Site 2 @0x38: target `addi r7,r29,0`, ours `li r7,0`. Site 3 @0x3c: target `addi r3,r29,0`, ours `li r3,0`. All three are class (b) in the lane's taxonomy - li-vs-copy, requiring a dominating-def proof - and none is class (a). BRANCH-TARGET AUDIT, run over the whole function on both streams: the only branch targets are 0x44 (the bdnz loop head), 0x70, 0x7c, 0x80 and 0xa0, every one of them at or after 0x44. All three sites therefore lie in the straight-line preheader, no back-edge can re-enter between the def and any use, and although r29 IS redefined inside the loop by `or r29,r29,r6` at 0x7c there is no path from there back to any site. DOMINATING-DEF PROOF, per site: site 1 is discharged by a ONE-INSTRUCTION backward scan - the def at 0x18 is the immediately preceding instruction, straight-line, with no interposed write to r29, no interposed branch target and no interposed call. Sites 2 and 3 carry one further obligation site 1 does not: `bl G3DGetPadStatusBuffer` sits at 0x24, BETWEEN the def and the uses. r29 is non-volatile (r14-r31) so the PPC EABI guarantees the callee preserves it, but that is an ABI argument rather than a local-scan argument, and a fail-closed guard should not silently assume it. RECOMMENDATION to the lane: have v1 of any li-vs-copy rule REFUSE any window containing a `bl`, which passes site 1 and defers sites 2 and 3, rather than encode a callee-saved assumption into the audit. ECONOMIC CORRECTION, the most important item here: closing all three form sites does NOT make this function exact. Two independent non-form residuals survive and neither is a form rewrite. First, a SCHEDULE swap of two adjacent independent instructions at 0x14/0x18 - target emits `li r29,0` then `addi r31,r3,LO`, ours emits them in the opposite order; the v2 record calls this a knock-on of the form difference, which is plausible but it is a genuine permutation that a rule must still account for. Second, a pure r6<->r8 RECOLOR - target `addi r8,r31,8` @0x28 and `srw r6,r5,r7` @0x4c against our `addi r6,r31,8` and `srw r8,r5,r7`, with knock-ons at `lwz r4,0(rX)` @0x44 and `or r29,r29,rX` @0x7c/0x84. So a matched% win on this function needs a COMPOSED form-plus-permute-plus-recolor rule, not the form rule alone; the form rule alone buys three rows out of twenty. DO NOT RETRY on the source axis: the v2 dead-lever list stands in full.
